# rusolve diagnostics

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_agent_docs.py from `rusolve --explain all` (the registry in crates/rusolve-core/src/diagnostic.rs). Do not edit; run the script. -->

Every error and warning has a stable code. `rusolve --explain RSnnnn` prints an entry; under `--format json` an error is a `rusolve.diagnostics/1` document on stdout ([schema](../schema/rusolve-diagnostics-1.schema.json)), the rustc-style text goes to stderr. API contract: [docs/design/diagnostics.md](../design/diagnostics.md).

### RS0001

**unknown command** (error)

The first argument is not a rusolve command. `rusolve --help` lists the commands (`rusolve --help --json` for the registry). The help line names the closest command when one is within a few edits, for example `slove` for `solve`.

### RS0002

**unknown flag** (error)

The command does not have this flag. `rusolve <command> --help` lists its flags. The help line names the closest flag when one is within a few edits, for example `--time-limt` for `--time-limit`. A flag that exists only on the other stack (HiGHS port or native/legacy) gets its own message naming the switch that selects that stack.

### RS0003

**missing or invalid flag value** (error)

A flag needs a value it did not get, got one of the wrong kind (a number expected, text given), one outside its list of choices, or was given twice although it takes one value. Other flag combinations the command refuses (`--csv` with `--format json`) also use this code. The message names the flag and what it expects; `rusolve <command> --help` shows the type and choices.

### RS0004

**unknown solver option** (error)

`--opt name=value`, `--options-file` or the MCP `options` map named an option the registry does not have, or gave a value it rejects. `rusolve options` lists every name with type, range and default. The help line names the closest option, for example `mip_rel_gapp` for `mip_rel_gap`.

### RS0005

**unknown environment variable** (error)

A `RUSOLVE_*` variable is set that no crate reads. A typo in such a name would silently change nothing (or the engine), so the CLI exits before running. `rusolve env` lists the registered variables; the help line names the closest. Prefer an option (`--opt`) over a variable.

### RS0006

**missing or unexpected argument** (error)

A command needs a model path it did not get, or got a positional argument it does not take. `rusolve <command> --help` shows the usage line.

### RS0010

**model or input file cannot be read** (error)

The model, solution, basis, options or hook file is missing, unreadable, or its format is not recognised. Check the path and the extension: MPS, LP, .nl and MathOptFormat JSON are read, optionally gzip, bzip2, xz or zstd compressed.

### RS0011

**model file does not parse** (error)

The file was read but its content is not a valid model in its format. The message carries the reader's own text; readers that report a file line and column point at it, with the declared names as help when a name is undeclared (RS1004). `rusolve convert` or a re-export from the modelling tool usually fixes a generated file.

### RS0012

**model is not supported by this command** (error)

The model parses but belongs to a class the command cannot solve (nonconvex or mixed-integer quadratic, mixed-integer conic, general constraints with quadratic terms, or a Hessian given to `mip`), or the model is outside what the selected engine takes (`mip_engine=cpsat` needs every column integer with finite bounds and integral rows, and an OR-Tools library that can be loaded at run time: `rusolve version --format json` shows `cpsat.available` and the places searched; install it with `install.sh --with-cpsat` or `pip install 'rusolve[cpsat]'`, or point `RUSOLVE_ORTOOLS_LIB` at the file). `rusolve classify <model>` names the class and the engine that would take it.

### RS0090

**internal error** (error)

The solver failed in a way that is not the caller's mistake: an unexpected solver status, a result file that cannot be written, or an internal invariant. Re-run with the same input and report it with the model and the command line; the exit code is 4.

### RS1004

**name used before it is declared** (error)

A model file refers to a row or column name that no ROWS or COLUMNS section declared (MPS), for example a COLUMNS entry on row `R7` when only `R1`..`R6` exist. The diagnostic points at the line and column of the name and lists the declared names as help. Declare the row, or fix the spelling; the help line suggests the closest declared name.

### RS1005

**value is not a number** (error)

A coefficient, right-hand side, range or bound in a model file is not a number the reader can parse (`abc`, `1,5`, `1e`). The diagnostic points at the token. Write decimals with a point and exponents as `1e6`; `inf` and `-inf` are accepted for bounds. The reader reports every such value in the file (up to 20), not only the first.

### RS1006

**model file syntax error** (error)

A model file breaks its format's grammar in a way no more specific code covers: an unknown section or bound type, a malformed row or expression, an invalid JSON document. The diagnostic points at the line and column (MathOptFormat: the JSON path) and quotes the reader's message. Structural errors end the list, because what follows would only be a cascade of the first; fix it and read again.

### RS2001

**weak big-M coefficient** (warning)

An integer column carries a coefficient far above what the row can ever use (the row's implied activity bound minus its side), so the LP relaxation is weaker than it needs to be and the coefficient is numerically risky. The warning names the row, the column and the tightest valid coefficient and bound. Source: coefficient tightening in Achterberg et al., Presolve reductions in mixed integer programming, INFORMS J. Computing 2020. `rusolve lint` lists every finding; `--no-warnings` silences the warning on solve and mip.

### RS2002

**wide coefficient range** (warning)

The constraint matrix mixes very large and very small nonzeros, which costs accuracy in the basis factorisation and the tolerances. The warning names the extremes. Rescale rows and columns (change units) so the nonzeros fall in about 1e-3 to 1e6. `rusolve lint` lists every finding; `--no-warnings` silences the warning.

### RS2003

**huge bound or free column** (warning)

A column has a very large finite bound, or is free and appears with no cost in a single row, so it does no work or invites unbounded values. Tighten huge bounds to the largest value the variable can take, or delete a free column singleton. `rusolve lint` lists every finding; `--no-warnings` silences the warning.

### RS2010

**model is infeasible** (warning)

The solve ended Infeasible. When cheap (a bounded post-solve budget shared with the relaxation re-solve) the diagnostic names an irreducible infeasible set of rows: dropping any one member makes the rest feasible, so one of them has to change. When the budget ran out first it names an infeasible subset instead: the message says 'a subset of' and a note says 'not reduced'. Those rows conflict, but not every one is needed; `rusolve explain` computes the irreducible set. When the LP relaxation is feasible the conflict involves integrality. Source: Chinneck and Dravnieks 1991, Locating minimal infeasible constraint sets in linear programs. `rusolve explain` verifies the set; `rusolve feasrelax` finds the cheapest relaxation.

### RS2011

**model is unbounded** (warning)

The solve ended Unbounded. When cheap the diagnostic names the columns of a primal ray: moving along it keeps every row satisfied and improves the objective without limit. Bound those columns or add the missing constraint. `rusolve explain` verifies the ray and prints the objective rate.

### RS2012

**returned solution violates a constraint** (warning)

The solution the solver returned violates a row or a column bound by more than 1e-6. The warning names the worst row and the count. Usually the model is badly scaled; `rusolve lint` shows where, and `rusolve check` re-verifies the solution independently of the solver. `--no-warnings` silences this warning.

### RS3001

**MCP tool argument is missing or invalid** (error)

An MCP tool call carried an argument that is absent, of the wrong type or out of range, or named no known tool. The message names the argument path (for example `variables[2].lb`) and what was expected; the tool's inputSchema in tools/list states the full shape. Fix the argument and call again; nothing was changed by the failed call.

### RS3002

**MCP model handle is unknown** (error)

The model_id given to an MCP tool names no loaded model, because it was never loaded, was freed with free_model, or the server restarted. Handles live only as long as the server process. Call load_model or build_model again and use the model_id it returns.

### RS4001

**invalid argument to a Python model-building call** (error)

A `rusolve.Model` method (add_var, add_constr, set_bounds, ...) got an argument it cannot use: bounds with lb above ub, a vector of the wrong length, an unknown sense, a NaN, a duplicate index. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError` (also a `ValueError`) whose `.diagnostics[0].location` is the line of your code that made the call. The message names the argument; the docstring of the method lists what it accepts. Fix the argument and call again; the model is unchanged when a call raises.

### RS4002

**row or column index out of range in a Python call** (error)

An index passed to a `rusolve.Model`, `Vars` or `Solution` call is below zero or at least the number of rows or columns added so far. Python raises `rusolve.ModelIndexError` (also an `IndexError`). Indices count from 0 in the order the rows or columns were added; `m.num_rows` and `m.num_cols` give the limits. A row index from before a failed call may be stale because a failing `add_constrs` removes the rows it had added.

### RS4003

**variables of two different Models combined** (error)

A Var, LinExpr or Constraint made from one `rusolve.Model` was used with another Model, or a Solution of one Model was indexed with a Var of another. Indices are only meaningful inside their own Model, so mixing them would silently read the wrong column. Create the expression from the Model it is added to, or index the Solution with variables of the Model that produced it. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError`.

### RS4004

**the model is infeasible (Python)** (error)

`Solution.raise_for_status()` found status Infeasible: no assignment satisfies every row and bound. Python raises `rusolve.InfeasibleError`. `Model.explain()` returns an irreducible infeasible subsystem (a small set of rows and bounds that conflict), with the Python line that added each row when `Model.capture_source` is on. `Model.feasrelax()` finds the cheapest relaxation that makes the model feasible.

### RS4005

**the model is unbounded or infeasible-or-unbounded (Python)** (error)

`Solution.raise_for_status()` found status Unbounded or InfeasibleOrUnbounded: the objective can improve without limit, or presolve could not tell that from infeasibility. Python raises `rusolve.UnboundedError`. `Model.explain()` returns the unbounded ray or the infeasible subsystem. Usually a bound or a constraint is missing on the variables the ray moves along; re-solving with `presolve=False` separates the two cases.

### RS4006

**the solve stopped without an optimal solution (Python)** (error)

`Solution.raise_for_status()` found a status other than Optimal, Infeasible or Unbounded: a time, iteration, node or solution limit, an interrupt, or an internal error. Python raises `rusolve.LimitError`. When `Solution.ok` is true the best primal solution found so far is in `Solution.x` with its gap in `Solution.gap`. Raise `time_limit` (or the named limit) to continue, or relax the gap.

### RS4007

**no primal solution to read (Python)** (error)

A value was read from a `Solution` that has no primal vector, for example `sol[var]` after an infeasible solve (`sol.x` and `sol.duals` are None when there is no solution, they do not raise). Python raises `rusolve.NoSolutionError` (also a `ValueError`). Check `Solution.ok` before reading values, or call `Solution.raise_for_status()` to get the typed error for the status.

### RS4008

**a Python callback hook raised an exception** (error)

A hook of the object passed as `Model.solve(callback=...)` (on_progress, on_improving_solution, on_cut_pool, user_solution, separate, branching_score, select_node, lazy_constraints) raised, or returned a value of the wrong type or length. The solver never sees the exception: the first one is kept, no later hook is called (each falls back to the solver's own rule), the solve is interrupted at its next limit check and `Model.solve` raises `rusolve.CallbackError` whose `__cause__` is the original exception and whose `.solution` is the partial result. `Model.callback_stats` counts calls and errors per hook. Fix the hook: it must return what its docstring names (a list of cuts, one score per candidate, an index into `ctx.open_nodes`, a full-length solution or None).

### RS4009

**invalid general constraint in a Python call** (error)

A `Model.add_indicator`, `add_sos1`, `add_sos2`, `add_pwl`, `add_abs`, `add_min`, `add_max`, `add_and`, `add_or` or `add_not` call got an object the solver cannot take: an indicator variable that is not binary (it needs integer bounds within [0, 1]), an indicator row that is a range, breakpoints that are fewer than two, of different lengths or not sorted by x, SOS weights of the wrong length, an operand count the function does not allow, a variable that does not exist, or a non-binary variable in `add_and`, `add_or` or `add_not`. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError` (also a `ValueError`) naming the object; the model is unchanged when a call raises. A later `set_bounds` or `set_integer` can make an object invalid: `Model.solve` then raises the same code before solving.

### RS4010

**a Python call does not support the model's general constraints** (error)

The model has indicator, SOS, piecewise-linear, abs/min/max or and/or/not objects, and the call (`explain`, `iis`, `ranging`, `feasrelax`, `diagnose`, `lint(with_solve=True)`, a `solve` callback or a quadratic objective) would work on the plain rows and silently ignore them, which gives a wrong answer. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError` instead. `solve`, `check` and `write` support these objects: `check` evaluates them on your objects with binaries rounded, and `write` keeps them in the LP or MPS file. To diagnose infeasibility, replace the objects by their big-M rows with the same model written by hand, or relax them one at a time.

### RS4011

**invalid scheduling or combinatorial (CP) object** (error)

A `Model.add_interval`, `add_no_overlap`, `add_cumulative`, `add_all_different`, `add_element` or `add_table` call (or an entry of the `cp` section of the MCP `build_model` tool) got an object the solver cannot take. The message names the object and what is wrong: a variable that does not exist, is not integer or has an infinite bound (every variable of a CP object is an integer with finite bounds), a presence variable that is not binary, a negative size, demand or capacity (or a variable that can be negative), an interval index that is out of range or listed twice, demands that do not match the intervals, a table tuple of the wrong length, an element with no values. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError` (also a `ValueError`); `build_model` returns an error naming the JSON path, for example `cp.no_overlap[0].intervals[2]`. The model is unchanged when a call raises. A later `set_bounds` or `set_integer` can make an object invalid: `Model.solve` then raises the same code before solving. No MPS or LP file carries these objects.

### RS4012

**a call does not support the model's CP objects** (error)

The model has scheduling or combinatorial objects (interval, no-overlap, cumulative, all-different, element, table), and the call (`explain`, `iis`, `ranging`, `feasrelax`, `diagnose`, `lint(with_solve=True)`, a `solve` callback, a quadratic objective, or the MCP tools `modify`, `explain`, `lint`, `ranging`, `feasrelax` on such a model) would work on the plain rows and silently ignore them, which gives a wrong answer. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError`; the MCP tool returns an error. `solve` and `check` support these objects: `check` evaluates them on your objects. To diagnose infeasibility, relax or remove the objects one at a time.

### RS4013

**the MIP linearization cannot take a CP object** (error)

The object is valid, but the engine-free fallback (the MIP linearization of the CP layer) refuses it, and no other engine is available. The message names the object and the limit: a cumulative whose horizon (from the start and end bounds) exceeds the time-indexed limit (1000 time points) or whose sizes or demands are variables, a no-overlap interval whose size variable can be 0, a derived big-M above 1e6, or a domain too large to enumerate (more than 100000 value, tuple or start-time binaries). Tighten the variable bounds, make sizes and demands constants, or use the CP-SAT engine, which takes these models without a limit when it is installed. Python raises `rusolve.ModelError`; the MCP `solve` tool returns an error.
